Senses.PreferredTarget: revile the buddhas and curse the patriarchs
AlternateTargets: scold the buddhas and abuse the patriarchs

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To revile buddhas and curse patriarchs is a named act of verbal attack on the tradition’s highest figures; records use it as conduct, answer, prediction, appraisal, and self-description.
EvidenceBody: Yangqi Fanghui uses a close rebuke-graph variant in a hall saying. Zhenjing Kewen applies the exact expression to Deshan; Yulin Tongxiu imagines withdrawing to a solitary peak to do it; and Guishan Lingyou predicts that Deshan will live on a solitary peak and do it.

Later public questions receive it as an answer, Baoning Renyong includes it among acts that make a great buddha-work, and Zhenjing both questions what fault lies in Deshan’s conduct and says he himself will go do it. Approval, criticism, prediction, and quotation change stance, not the named act.

Senses.Note: Eleven stored evidence rows remain after governed graphic variants are retained; C077n1710 and D48n8939 are treated as editions of one work rather than independent works.
